description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for five different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, and MEMIT, as evaluated in the context of editing large language models for long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 80%, with major gridlines at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The “Base” method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 63% ACC at co-occurrence 1 and gradually increases to about 68.5% at 10⁴. The “FT” method (blue line with downward triangle markers) begins near 64% and rises to roughly 70.5%. The “IKE” method (red line with upward triangle markers) starts at ~66% and reaches ~72.5%. The “MEND” method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~69% and climbs to ~77%. The “MEMIT” method (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at ~68.5% and increases to ~75%. The “MEND” and “MEMIT” lines are consistently above the others across the entire range, with “MEND” showing the highest overall performance, reaching approximately 82% ACC at the highest co-occurrence number shown (around 5×10³). All lines exhibit a generally increasing trend, indicating improved accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers, though the rate of improvement varies by method.
